facts.statement: Austroraptor lived during the Late Cretaceous period in the Allen Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: known from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian–Maastrichtian ages) Allen Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: Austroraptor was a large, bipedal carnivore that measured between 5 and 6 meters in length and weighed between 300 and 520 kilograms.
facts.quote: measuring around 5 - 6 m long and weighing up to 300 - 520 kg.

facts.statement: Austroraptor is one of the largest known paravian dinosaurs, comparable in size only to large dromaeosaurids like Achillobator and Utahraptor.
facts.quote: It is one of the largest paravians known, with only large dromaeosaurids such as Achillobator and Utahraptor approaching a similar size.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Austroraptor was found in the Bajo de Santa Rosa locality within the Allen Formation in Río Negro, Argentina.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Austroraptor cabazai, holotype MML-195, was recovered in the Bajo de Santa Rosa locality of the Allen Formation, in Río Negro, Argentina.

facts.statement: The species Austroraptor cabazai was formally named and described in 2008 by Fernando Emilio Novas and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2008, the type species Austroraptor cabazai was named and described by Fernando Emilio Novas, Diego Pol, Juan Canale, Juan Porfiri and Jorge Calvo.

facts.statement: The name Austroraptor translates to "Southern Thief," combining Latin words for south wind and thief.
facts.quote: The genus name Austroraptor means "Southern Thief," and is derived from the Latin word auster meaning "the south wind" and the Latin word raptor meaning "thief."

facts.statement: Austroraptor possessed a low, elongated skull measuring 80 centimeters in length, which was more elongated than those of other dromaeosaurs.
facts.quote: The skull is low and elongated, much more so than that of other dromaeosaurs, and measures 80 cm.

facts.statement: Austroraptor had conical, non-serrated teeth with fluted enamel, a feature compared to those of spinosaurids.
facts.quote: Austroraptor has conical, non-serrated teeth, which Novas et al. compared to those of spinosaurids, based on how the enamel of the surface of its teeth is fluted.

facts.statement: Some researchers have hypothesized that the holotype specimen of Austroraptor might be a paleontological chimera, though this remains unproven.
facts.quote: This has suggested to some researchers that the holotype specimen is a paleontological chimera; however, there is no uncertainty about the affinity of the taxon, so a chimera hypothesis can not be assured.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Austroraptor within the subfamily Unenlagiinae of the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis of the holotype specimen's anatomical features by the describers placed Austroraptor within the subfamily Unenlagiinae of Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that unenlagiines like Austroraptor had superior running and pursuit predation capabilities compared to other dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that unenlagiines had better capacities for running and pursuit predation than other dromaeosaurids.

facts.statement: In 2021, Brum and colleagues proposed that Austroraptor likely consumed fish as a significant or primary part of its diet, based on its non-serrated conical teeth resembling those of piscivorous tetrapods.
facts.quote: In 2021, Brum and colleagues suggested that unenlagiines such as Austroraptor and its sister taxon Ypupiara likely consumed fish for a considerable part of their diet, possibly even as a main food source, based on their non-serrated conical teeth that are similar to those of piscivorous tetrapods including gavialoids, spinosaurids, anhanguerids, etc.

facts.statement: Austroraptor lived during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was found in terrestrial sediments that were deposited during the Campanian–Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. estimated that Austroraptor lived between 78 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. has estimated that Austroraptor lived between 78 million and 66 million years ago, until the end of the Mesozoic era.

facts.statement: Austroraptor was a medium-sized bipedal hunter that could grow up to 6.2 meters long and weigh 340 kilograms.
facts.quote: Austroraptor era un dinosaurio cazador bípedo de proporciones medias, que podría crecer hasta 6.2 metros de largo y con 340 kilogramos de peso corporal.

facts.statement: Austroraptor is one of the largest known dromaeosaurids, surpassed only by Achillobator, Dakotaraptor, and Utahraptor, and it is the largest dromaeosaurid discovered in the Southern Hemisphere.
facts.quote: Su tamaño hace de Austroraptor uno de los dromeosáuridos más grandes conocidos, con sólo el Achillobator, Dakotaraptor y Utahraptor acercándose en tamaño, siendo el más grande en ser descubierto en el hemisferio sur.

facts.statement: A notable feature of Austroraptor was its relatively short forearms compared to most members of its group.
facts.quote: Algo particularmente notable acerca del taxón eran los relativamente cortos antebrazos, de una proporción mucho menor, en comparación con la mayoría de los miembros de su grupo.

facts.statement: Austroraptor had a long, low snout with numerous small, conical teeth, a condition similar to spinosaurids.
facts.quote: Su hocico es largo y bajo, con numerosos dientes pequeños y cónicos, una condición que se asemeja a los espinosáuridos.

facts.statement: A. cabazai measures around 6.2 meters long from head to tail.
facts.quote: Considerado grande para ser un dromeosáurido, A. cabazai mide alrededor de 6.2 metros de largo desde la cabeza hasta la cola.

facts.statement: Austroraptor's skull was 80 centimeters long, low, and elongated, much longer than those of other dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Su cráneo de 80 centímetros de largo es bajo y alargado, mucho más que los de otros dromeosáuridos.

facts.statement: Among dromaeosaurids, only A. cabazai, Tianyuraptor, and Mahakala have similarly reduced forelimbs.
facts.quote: Entre los dromeosáuridos solamente A. cabazai, Tianyuraptor y Mahakala tienen extremidades anteriores reducidas de manera similar.

facts.statement: Austroraptor's maxillary and dentary teeth were small, conical, lacked serrated edges, and had grooves, suggesting a piscivorous diet.
facts.quote: Los dientes maxilares y dentarios son pequeños, cónicos, desprovistos del borde aserrado para rasgar carne, y provistos de surcos, como en Buitreraptor, lo que sugiere una alimentación piscívora.

facts.statement: Some researchers have suggested that the holotype specimen of Austroraptor may be a chimera, meaning its bones could belong to more than one individual.
facts.quote: Esto ha sugerido a algunos investigadores que el espécimen holotipo es una quimera, lo que significa que sus huesos pueden ser de más de un individuo.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected in 2002 by Fernando Novas's team from the Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales in the Bajo de Santa Rosa of the Allen Formation, near Lamarque, Río Negro Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue recogido en 2002 por el equipo de Fernando Novas del Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales en el Bajo de Santa Rosa de la formación Allen, aproximadamente a 90 al sur oeste del pueblo de Lamarque, Provincia del Río Negro, Argentina.

facts.statement: The species Austroraptor cabazai was named and described in 2008 by Fernando Novas, Diego Pol, Juan Canale, Juan Porfiri, and Jorge Calvo.
facts.quote: En 2008, la especie tipo Austroraptor cabazai fue nombrado y descrito por Fernando Novas Emilio, Diego Pol, Juan Canale, Juan Porfiri y Jorge Calvo.

facts.statement: In 2012, Phil Currie and Ariana Paulina-Carabajal referenced a second specimen, MML-220, found in 2008.
facts.quote: Phil Currie y Ariana Paulina-Carabajal en el año 2012 se hace referencia a un segundo espécimen, MML-220, que se encontró en 2008.

facts.statement: The genus Austroraptor was established by Novas, Pol, Canale, Porfiri, and Calvo in 2008.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Novas, Pol, Canale, Porfiri y Calvo, 2008

facts.statement: The species A. cabazai was described by Novas, Pol, Canale, Porfiri, and Calvo in 2008.
facts.quote: species_authority: Novas, Pol, Canale, Porfiri y Calvo 2008

facts.statement: A cladistic analysis by its describers placed Austroraptor within the subfamily Unenlagiinae of Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico de las características anatómicas de Austroraptor realizado por los descriptores lo coloca dentro de la subfamilia Unenlagiinae de Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: The discovery of Austroraptor suggests that large coelurosaurs became common in the Late Cretaceous after the dominance of carcharodontosaurids declined.
facts.quote: The discovery of Austroraptor increases the understanding of ecological and morphological diversity among unenlagiines, demonstrating that members of the subfamily included giant short-armed and small long-armed members, and suggesting that during the end of the Cretaceous large coelurosaurs became common after the decreasing dominance of carcharodontosaurids.

facts.statement: The holotype MML-195 consists of various skull bones, cervical and dorsal vertebrae, ribs, gastralia, and limb bones including the right humerus, left pubis, left femur, and right tibia.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MML-195, consiste en los huesos frontal y postorbital derechos, los lacrimales, maxilares y dentarios con los dientes, surangular derecho y prearticular, las vértebras cervicales 3, 5, 6, 7 y 8, dorsales 2 y 4 y costillas y gastralias aisladas, húmero derecho, ungular manual del dígito III, pubis izquierdo, fémur izquierdo, y tibia, astrágalo, calcáneo, el metatarso III y las falanges I-2 del pedal, II-2, III-4 e IV-2 derechos.

facts.statement: In 2012, comparison with a second sample showed that the fourth toe was not especially wide and the supposed second phalanx was actually a first phalanx.
facts.quote: En 2012, la comparación con una segunda muestra mostró que el cuarto dedo del pie no era especialmente amplio, la segunda falange pretendida había sido de hecho una primera falange.

facts.statement: Austroraptor is the youngest record of dromaeosaurids found in Gondwana.
facts.quote: Este nuevo dinosaurio es el registro más joven de dromeosáuridos de Gondwana

facts.statement: Austroraptor represents a previously unknown lineage of large predators in the late Cretaceous fauna, which was dominated mainly by abelisaurids.
facts.quote: Este nuevo dinosaurio es el registro más joven de dromeosáuridos de Gondwana y representa un linaje previamente desconocido de depredadores grandes en la fauna del último cretáceo, dominadas principalmente por los abelisáuridos

facts.statement: The specimen was found in terrestrial sediments deposited during the Maastrichtian stage of the Cretaceous period, approximately 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue encontrado en sedimentos terrestres que se depositaron durante el Maastrichtiano última etapa del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años

facts.statement: Austroraptor shared its paleoenvironment with early mammals, pterosaurs, and the titanosaurs Saltasaurus and Rocasaurus, which may have served as prey for this dromaeosaurid.
facts.quote: Austroraptor compartió su paleoambiente con los mamíferos tempranos, pterosaurios y los titanosáuridos Saltasaurus y Rocasaurus, que pueden haber servido como presa para este dromeosáurido

facts.quote: Parent group: Unenlagiinae
